papers.title: Biological interpretation of baseline hepatitis B surface antigen and cirrhosis in determining interferon treatment duration
papers.abstract: The recent identification of baseline hepatitis B surface antigen and cirrhosis as independent predictors of extended interferon therapy provides a valuable clinical framework, yet the biological mechanisms underlying these associations require further elucidation. In this opinion review, we interpret these factors not merely as statistical covariates but as pathological surrogates for the virus-host equilibrium. We propose that high baseline hepatitis B surface antigen may reflect a deeply entrenched intrahepatic viral reservoir and may create an antigen-rich environment that impairs effective antiviral immunity. Concurrently, cirrhosis may be better understood as a spectrum of architectural remodeling in which vascular changes and sinusoidal defenestration could limit immune surveillance and affect local therapeutic access. Consequently, treatment durations exceeding 48 weeks may be required, at least in part, to overcome these profound immunological and structural barriers. We advocate shifting future predictive modeling from binary clinical definitions to a granular integration of viral kinetics and histological morphology to refine precision medicine in chronic hepatitis B.

analysis.summary_en: This review explores the biological interpretation of baseline hepatitis B surface antigen and cirrhosis as predictors of extended interferon therapy. It highlights the need to understand these factors as indicators of the virus-host equilibrium rather than just statistical covariates. The authors suggest that high hepatitis B surface antigen levels may signal an established viral reservoir that hampers immune responses, while cirrhosis is viewed as a structural change affecting immune surveillance and therapeutic access. papers.title: Predictive Value of Laboratory, Radiological, and Non-invasive Tests for Liver Biopsy Findings in Treatment-naive, HBeAg-negative Chronic Hepatitis B Patients
papers.abstract: Aim: Chronic hepatitis B (CHB) remains a major cause of liver-related morbidity and mortality worldwide.Liver biopsy is considered the reference standard for assessing significant histopathological abnormality (SHA); however, its invasive nature and potential complications limit routine use.This study aimed to evaluate the diagnostic performance of laboratory, radiological, and non-invasive indices in predicting significant histopathological abnormalities in treatment-naïve, HBeAg-negative CHB patients. Materials and Methods:In this retrospective single-center study, adult HBeAg-negative, treatment-naïve CHB patients who underwent liver biopsy between 2010 and 2024 were evaluated.Liver histology was assessed using the Ishak fibrosis score and Knodell histological activity index (HAI).Significant histological activity was defined as HAI ≥6 and/or fibrosis stage ≥2.Several non-invasive indices were calculated.Multivariable logistic regression analyses were performed to identify independent predictors of high HAI and significant fibrosis.Diagnostic performance was assessed using ROC curve analysis.Results: A total of 148 patients were included.Higher hepatitis B virus DNA levels were independently associated with both high HAI [odds ratio (OR): 1.7 per log 10 increase, p=0.002] and significant fibrosis (OR: 1.3 per log 10 increase, p=0.044).Lower serum albumin levels were independently associated with high HAI (p=0.025).Among non-invasive markers, aspartate aminotransferase to platelet ratio index (APRI), showed the highest accuracy for predicting high HAI [area under the curve (AUC): 0.785; sensitivity 68.2%, specificity 85.0% at a cut-off >0.35].The KING score demonstrated the best performance for predicting significant fibrosis (AUC: 0.768; sensitivity 61.5%, specificity 87.8%).GUCI and Fibrosis-4 index also showed good discriminatory ability.Conclusion: Simple, routinely available non-invasive indices particularly APRI and KING scores demonstrate good diagnostic performance in identifying SHA in HBeAg-negative CHB patients.These tools may help reduce the need for liver biopsy in selected patients and support clinical decision-making, especially in settings where biopsy access is limited.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Chronic hepatitis B (CHB) remains a major cause of liver-related morbidity and mortality worldwide. Liver biopsy is considered the reference standard for assessing significant histopathological abnormality (SHA); however, its invasive nature and potential complications limit routine use.
analysis.study_design_and_population: In this retrospective single-center study, adult HBeAg-negative, treatment-naïve CHB patients who underwent liver biopsy between 2010 and 2024 were evaluated.
analysis.methods: Liver histology was assessed using the Ishak fibrosis score and Knodell histological activity index (HAI). Significant histological activity was defined as HAI ≥6 and/or fibrosis stage ≥2. Several non-invasive indices were calculated. Multivariable logistic regression analyses were performed to identify independent predictors of high HAI and significant fibrosis. Diagnostic performance was assessed using ROC curve analysis.
analysis.main_results: A total of 148 patients were included. Higher hepatitis B virus DNA levels were independently associated with both high HAI [odds ratio (OR): 1.7 per log 10 increase, p=0.002] and significant fibrosis (OR: 1.3 per log 10 increase, p=0.044). Lower serum albumin levels were independently associated with high HAI (p=0.025). Among non-invasive markers, aspartate aminotransferase to platelet ratio index (APRI) showed the highest accuracy for predicting high HAI [area under the curve (AUC): 0.785; sensitivity 68.2%, specificity 85.0% at a cut-off >0.35]. The KING score demonstrated the best performance for predicting significant fibrosis (AUC: 0.768; sensitivity 61.5%, specificity 87.8%). GUCI and Fibrosis-4 index also showed good discriminatory ability.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Simple, routinely available non-invasive indices particularly APRI and KING scores demonstrate good diagnostic performance in identifying SHA in HBeAg-negative CHB patients. These tools may help reduce the need for liver biopsy in selected patients and support clinical decision-making, especially in settings where biopsy access is limited.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings may inform the development of non-invasive diagnostic tools for monitoring liver disease progression in HBeAg-negative CHB patients, potentially improving access to care and reducing the risks associated with liver biopsy.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its retrospective design and single-center setting, which may affect generalizability. The evidence is moderate in strength due to these limitations.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to evaluate the diagnostic performance of laboratory, radiological, and non-invasive indices in predicting significant histopathological abnormalities in treatment-naïve, HBeAg-negative chronic hepatitis B patients. A retrospective single-center study included 148 patients who underwent liver biopsy between 2010 and 2024. Liver histology was assessed using the Ishak fibrosis score and Knodell histological activity index (HAI), with significant histological activity defined as HAI ≥6 and/or fibrosis stage ≥2. Higher hepatitis B virus DNA levels were independently associated with high HAI and significant fibrosis, while lower serum albumin levels were linked to high HAI. Non-invasive indices such as APRI and KING score showed good accuracy in predicting these outcomes. The study suggests that these non-invasive tools may help reduce the need for liver biopsy in selected patients, supporting clinical decision-making in resource-limited settings. However, the retrospective design and single-center nature limit generalizability, resulting in moderate evidence strength.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 慢性乙型肝炎(CHB)仍是全球范围内肝脏相关发病和死亡率的主要原因。肝活检被认为是评估显著组织病理学异常(SHA)的参考标准;然而,其侵入性和潜在并发症限制了常规应用。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 在这项回顾性单中心研究中,评估了2010年至2024年间接受肝活检的成人HBeAg阴性、治疗初治慢性乙型肝炎患者。
elements_zh.methods: 肝脏组织学采用Ishak纤维化评分和Knodell组织学活动指数(HAI)进行评估。显著的组织学活动定义为HAI≥6和/或纤维化阶段≥2。计算了多种非侵入性指标。采用多变量逻辑回归分析以确定高HAI和显著纤维化的独立预测因素。使用ROC曲线分析评估诊断性能。
elements_zh.main_results: 总共纳入了148例患者。较高的乙型肝炎病毒 DNA水平与高HAI[比值比(OR):每增加一个log 10单位为1.7,p=0.002]和显著纤维化[OR:每增加一个log 10单位为1.3,p=0.044]独立相关。较低的血清白蛋白水平与高HAI独立相关(p=0.025)。在非侵入性标志物中,天门冬氨酸氨基转移酶与血小板比值指数(APRI)在预测高HAI方面显示出最高的准确性[曲线下面积(AUC):0.785;在截断值>0.35时,灵敏度68.2%,特异度85.0%]。KING评分在预测显著纤维化方面表现最佳(AUC:0.768;灵敏度61.5%,特异度87.8%)。GUCI和Fibrosis-4指数也显示出良好的鉴别能力。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 简单、常规可得的非侵入性指标,特别是APRI和KING评分,在识别HBeAg阴性慢性乙型肝炎患者中的SHV方面表现出良好的诊断性能。这些工具可能有助于减少特定患者对肝活检的需求,并支持临床决策,尤其是在活检获取受限的环境中。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可能有助于开发非侵入性诊断工具,用于监测HBeAg阴性慢性乙型肝炎患者肝病的进展,从而 potentially 提高医疗服务的可及性并降低肝穿刺相关的风险。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究受到其回顾性设计和单中心设置的限制,这可能会影响其普遍适用性。由于这些限制,证据强度中等。

papers.abstract_zh: 目的:慢性乙型肝炎(CHB)仍然是导致肝相关疾病的主要原因。肝活检被认为是评估显著组织病理异常(SHA)的参考标准;然而,其侵入性和潜在并发症限制了其常规使用。本研究旨在评估实验室、影像学和非侵入性指标在预测治疗-naïve、HBeAg阴性CHB患者显著组织病理异常方面的诊断性能。材料与方法:在2010年至2024年间进行肝活检的成人HBeAg阴性、治疗-naïve CHB患者中进行回顾性单中心研究。使用Ishak纤维化评分和Knodell组织学活动指数(HAI)评估肝组织学。显著组织学活动被定义为HAI≥6和/或纤维化阶段≥2。计算了多个非侵入性指标。进行了多元logistic回归分析以确定高HAI和显著纤维化的独立预测因子。使用ROC曲线分析评估诊断性能。结果:共纳入148名患者。较高的乙型肝炎病毒 DNA水平与高HAI [每增加10倍对数值比值比(OR):1.7,p=0.002]和显著纤维化(每增加10倍对数值比值比:1.3,p=0.044)独立相关。较低的血清白蛋白水平与高HAI独立相关(p=0.025)。在非侵入性标志物中,天冬氨酸转氨酶与血小板比率指数(APRI)在预测高HAI方面表现出最高的准确性 [曲线下面积(AUC):0.785;灵敏度68.2%,特异性85.0%在截断值>0.35]。KING评分在预测显著纤维化方面表现出最佳性能(AUC:0.768;灵敏度61.5%,特异性87.8%)。GUCI和纤维化-4指数也显示出良好的区分能力。结论:简单的、常规可用的非侵入性指标,特别是APRI和KING评分,在识别HBeAg阴性CHB患者的SHA方面表现出良好的诊断性能。这些工具可能有助于减少特定患者进行肝活检的需求,并支持临床决策,特别是在活检获取受限的情况下。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 慢性乙型肝炎(CHB)仍是全球范围内肝脏相关发病和死亡率的主要原因。肝活检被认为是评估显著组织病理学异常(SHA)的参考标准;然而,其侵入性和潜在并发症限制了常规应用。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 在这项回顾性单中心研究中,评估了2010年至2024年间接受肝活检的成人HBeAg阴性、治疗初治慢性乙型肝炎患者。
analysis_zh.methods: 肝脏组织学采用Ishak纤维化评分和Knodell组织学活动指数(HAI)进行评估。显著的组织学活动定义为HAI≥6和/或纤维化阶段≥2。计算了多种非侵入性指标。采用多变量逻辑回归分析以确定高HAI和显著纤维化的独立预测因素。使用ROC曲线分析评估诊断性能。
analysis_zh.main_results: 总共纳入了148例患者。较高的乙型肝炎病毒 DNA水平与高HAI[比值比(OR):每增加一个log 10单位为1.7,p=0.002]和显著纤维化[OR:每增加一个log 10单位为1.3,p=0.044]独立相关。较低的血清白蛋白水平与高HAI独立相关(p=0.025)。在非侵入性标志物中,天门冬氨酸氨基转移酶与血小板比值指数(APRI)在预测高HAI方面显示出最高的准确性[曲线下面积(AUC):0.785;在截断值>0.35时,灵敏度68.2%,特异度85.0%]。KING评分在预测显著纤维化方面表现最佳(AUC:0.768;灵敏度61.5%,特异度87.8%)。GUCI和Fibrosis-4指数也显示出良好的鉴别能力。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 简单、常规可得的非侵入性指标,特别是APRI和KING评分,在识别HBeAg阴性慢性乙型肝炎患者中的SHV方面表现出良好的诊断性能。这些工具可能有助于减少特定患者对肝活检的需求,并支持临床决策,尤其是在活检获取受限的环境中。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可能有助于开发非侵入性诊断工具,用于监测HBeAg阴性慢性乙型肝炎患者肝病的进展,从而 potentially 提高医疗服务的可及性并降低肝穿刺相关的风险。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究受到其回顾性设计和单中心设置的限制,这可能会影响其普遍适用性。由于这些限制,证据强度中等。

papers.title: MAFLD is linked to lower HBV DNA levels in chronic hepatitis B: clinical and transcriptomic insights
papers.abstract: Background Chronic hepatitis B (CHB) frequently coexists with metabolic dysfunction–associated fatty liver disease (MAFLD), yet the impact of MAFLD on hepatitis B virus (HBV) replication remains incompletely understood. We aimed to investigate the association between MAFLD and HBV DNA levels and to provide biological context through integrative transcriptomic analyses. Methods We analyzed a large retrospective cohort of patients with CHB and assessed the association between MAFLD and serum HBV DNA levels using linear regression models. HBV DNA was analyzed as a continuous outcome after log10 transformation. To provide molecular context for the clinical findings, weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) was performed in an independent HBV liver transcriptomic dataset to identify HBV-associated host co-expression modules. These modules were subsequently characterized in independent liver transcriptomic datasets representing distinct metabolic and histological liver contexts using single-sample gene set enrichment analysis (ssGSEA). Results MAFLD was independently associated with lower circulating HBV DNA levels. This association varied across MAFLD phenotypes, with the lowest HBV DNA levels observed in overweight- or obesity-related MAFLD. Transcriptomic analyses identified HBV-associated host co-expression programs linked to lipid and cholesterol metabolism, inflammatory signaling, and antiviral responses. Cross-cohort analyses further showed that selected modules varied across distinct metabolic and fibrotic liver contexts. Conclusions MAFLD is associated with reduced HBV DNA levels in patients with CHB, especially in overweight- or obesity-related MAFLD. The transcriptomic findings provide complementary biological context for this clinical association and highlight metabolic and immune pathways that warrant further mechanistic investigation.

papers.abstract_zh: 背景:慢性乙型肝炎(慢性乙型肝炎)常与代谢功能障碍相关脂肪肝病(MAFLD)共存,但MAFLD对乙型肝炎病毒(HBV)复制的影响仍不完全明确。我们旨在探讨MAFLD与HBV DNA水平之间的关联,并通过整合转录组学分析提供生物学背景。方法:我们分析了慢性乙型肝炎患者的大型回顾性队列研究,并使用线性回归模型评估MAFLD与血清HBV DNA水平之间的关联。HBV DNA在log10转换后作为连续变量进行分析。为提供临床发现的分子背景,我们在独立的HBV肝脏转录组学数据集中进行了加权基因共表达网络分析(WGCNA),以识别与HBV相关的宿主共表达模块。随后,使用单样本基因集富集分析(ssGSEA)在代表不同代谢和组织学肝脏背景的独立肝脏转录组学数据集中对这些模块进行了特征分析。结果:MAFLD与较低的循环HBV DNA水平独立相关。这种关联在MAFLD的不同表型中有所差异,其中与超重或肥胖相关的MAFLD观察到最低的HBV DNA水平。转录组学分析识别出与脂质和胆固醇代谢、炎症信号传导以及抗病毒药物反应相关的HBV相关宿主共表达程序。跨队列研究分析进一步表明,所选模块在不同的代谢和纤维化肝脏背景下有所变化。结论:MAFLD与慢性乙型肝炎患者中的HBV DNA水平降低相关,尤其是在与超重或肥胖相关的MAFLD中。转录组学发现为这一临床关联提供了补充的生物学背景,并突出了需要进一步机制研究的代谢和免疫通路。科学与公共卫生意义:这些发现表明MAFLD可能影响HBV复制,并可能为未来研究该关联的分子机制提供信息,从而指导针对慢性乙型肝炎和MAFLD患者的靶向干预措施。局限性与证据强度:本研究基于回顾性队列研究,这可能引入偏倚并限制因果推断。由于研究的观察性质以及潜在的混杂因素,证据强度中等。

analysis_zh.main_results: MAFLD与较低的循环HBV DNA水平独立相关。这种关联在MAFLD的不同表型中有所差异,其中与超重或肥胖相关的MAFLD观察到最低的HBV DNA水平。跨队列研究分析进一步表明,所选模块在不同的代谢和纤维化肝脏背景下有所变化。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: MAFLD与慢性乙型肝炎患者中的HBV DNA水平降低相关,尤其是在与超重或肥胖相关的MAFLD中。转录组学发现为这一临床关联提供了补充的生物学背景,并突出了需要进一步机制研究的代谢和免疫通路。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现表明MAFLD可能影响HBV复制,并可能为未来研究该关联的分子机制提供信息,从而指导针对慢性乙型肝炎和MAFLD患者的靶向干预措施。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究基于回顾性队列研究,这可能引入偏倚并限制因果推断。由于研究的观察性质以及潜在的混杂因素,证据强度中等。

papers.title: Seroprotection Status of Hepatitis B Vaccination Among Healthcare Workers in a Tertiary Care Hospital: A Cross-Sectional Study
papers.abstract: Abstract Background: Healthcare workers (HCWs) are at increased occupational risk of hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection due to frequent exposure to blood and body fluids. Hepatitis B vaccination is highly effective; however, antibody levels may wane over time, leaving some vaccinated individuals unprotected. Periodic assessment of anti-hepatitis B surface antibody (anti-HBs) titers is, therefore, essential. Materials and Methods: A cross-sectional study was conducted from September to December 2025 at Government Theni Medical College, Theni. A total of 146 HCWs were enrolled. Demographic details and vaccination history were recorded using a structured proforma. Serum anti-HBs titers were estimated by the enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay. Seroprotection was defined as anti-HBs ≥10 mIU/mL. Data were analyzed using Statistical Package for the Social Sciences version 24.0. The chi-square test was used to assess associations, and P value < 0.05 was considered statistically significant. Results: Of the 146 HCWs, 108 (74.0%) were vaccinated and 38 (26.0%) were unvaccinated. Protective anti-HBs titers were observed in 78.7% of vaccinated HCWs. Seroprotection was significantly lower among housekeeping staff and in older age groups. Among unvaccinated HCWs, 26.3% demonstrated protective anti-HBs titers, suggesting previous natural exposure. Conclusion: Although vaccination coverage among HCWs was relatively good, a considerable proportion of them lacked protective antibody levels. These findings support strengthening hepatitis B vaccination programs and post-vaccination serological assessment among high-risk HCWs. Booster vaccination may be considered for individuals with nonprotective anti-HB titers according to the current guidelines.

papers.title_zh: 三级医院医护人员乙型肝炎疫苗疫苗接种的血清保护状态:横断面研究
papers.source_body_en: Abstract Background: Healthcare workers (HCWs) are at increased occupational risk of hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection due to frequent exposure to blood and body fluids. Hepatitis B vaccination is highly effective; however, antibody levels may wane over time, leaving some vaccinated individuals unprotected. Periodic assessment of anti-hepatitis B surface antibody (anti-HBs) titers is, therefore, essential. Materials and Methods: A cross-sectional study was conducted from September to December 2025 at Government Theni Medical College, Theni. A total of 146 HCWs were enrolled. Demographic details and vaccination history were recorded using a structured proforma. Serum anti-HBs titers were estimated by the enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay. Seroprotection was defined as anti-HBs ≥10 mIU/mL. Data were analyzed using Statistical Package for the Social Sciences version 24.0. The chi-square test was used to assess associations, and P value < 0.05 was considered statistically significant. Results: Of the 146 HCWs, 108 (74.0%) were vaccinated and 38 (26.0%) were unvaccinated. Protective anti-HBs titers were observed in 78.7% of vaccinated HCWs. Seroprotection was significantly lower among housekeeping staff and in older age groups. Among unvaccinated HCWs, 26.3% demonstrated protective anti-HBs titers, suggesting previous natural exposure. Conclusion: Although vaccination coverage among HCWs was relatively good, a considerable proportion of them lacked protective antibody levels. These findings support strengthening hepatitis B vaccination programs and post-vaccination serological assessment among high-risk HCWs. Booster vaccination may be considered for individuals with nonprotective anti-HB titers according to the current guidelines.
papers.abstract_zh: 摘要 背景:由于频繁接触血液和体液,医护人员(HCWs)面临更高的职业性乙型肝炎病毒(HBV)感染风险。乙型肝炎疫苗接种具有高度有效性;然而,抗体水平可能随时间下降,使部分接种者失去保护。因此,定期评估抗乙型肝炎表面抗体(anti-HBs)滴度至关重要。材料和方法:2025年9月至12月期间,在Government Theni Medical College,Theni进行了一项横断面研究。共纳入146名HCWs。使用结构化表格记录了人口学信息和疫苗接种接种史。通过酶联免疫吸附试验(ELISA)估计血清anti-HBs滴度。血清保护定义为anti-HBs ≥10 mIU/mL。数据使用SPSS 24.0版进行分析。采用卡方检验评估相关性,P值<0.05被认为具有统计学意义。结果:在146名HCWs中,108名(74.0%)接种了疫苗接种,38名(26.0%)未接种。接种疫苗接种的HCWs中有78.7%表现出保护性anti-HBs滴度。血清保护率在清洁工和年龄较大的群体中显著降低。在未接种疫苗接种的HCWs中,26.3%表现出保护性anti-HBs滴度,提示可能有既往自然暴露。结论:尽管HCWs的疫苗接种接种率相对较高,但相当一部分人缺乏保护性抗体水平。这些发现支持加强乙型肝炎疫苗接种接种计划,并对高风险HCWs进行接种后血清学评估。根据当前指南,对于anti-HB滴度不具保护性的个体,可考虑加强接种疫苗接种。

papers.title: Screening of Hepatitis B and C Viral Infection among Pregnant Women in Fallujah Teaching Hospital for Maternity and Children
papers.abstract: Background: Viral hepatitis is a global health burden and an endemic infection in Iraq, with its incidence previously documented. Aim: This study aimed to delineate the current prevalence of hepatitis during pregnancy in comparison with previous local data and to determine plausible risk factors associated with the outcome. Methods: A total of 1273 participants were recruited in this hospital-based cross-sectional study from 1 February to 30 June 2024. The cohort consisted of pregnant women aged 14–45 years. Demographic data were collected using a short questionnaire to assess potential risk factors for viral hepatitis. Blood samples were collected to screen for hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) and antibodies to hepatitis C virus (anti-HCV) using Combo Rapid Test Strips. Results: The results revealed that the overall prevalence of viral hepatitis infection among pregnant women was 1.02%, with HBV occurring more frequently than HCV. The seroprevalence of HBsAg among pregnant women was 0.94% (12/1273). The current study reported a notable decline in HBV and HCV infection among pregnant women compared with a previous local study (0.94% vs 4.42% for HBV and 0.08% vs 1.15% for HCV). Logistic regression analysis revealed that both family history of hepatitis and abortion were associated with significantly higher odds of HBV (OR = 12.77 at P = 0.001 and OR = 9.24 at P = 0.0009) compared with their counterparts. Conclusion: Family history of hepatitis and history of abortion were significantly associated with HBV seropositivity among pregnant women, supporting the implementation of robust prenatal screening procedures and greater awareness of disease outcomes.
papers.journal: Asian Journal of Research in Infectious Diseases

papers.abstract_zh: 背景:病毒性肝炎是全球健康负担,也是伊拉克的流行病,其患病率之前已有记录。目的:本研究旨在明确孕妇在妊娠期间肝炎的当前血清流行率,并与以往的本地数据进行比较,同时确定与结果相关的潜在风险因素。方法:本研究是一项基于医院的横断面研究,于2024年2月1日至6月30日期间招募了1273名参与者。研究对象为14至45岁的孕妇。通过简短的问卷收集人口统计数据,以评估病毒性肝炎的潜在风险因素。使用Combo Rapid Test Strips对血液样本进行检测,以筛查乙型肝炎病毒表面抗原(HBsAg)和丙型肝炎病毒抗体(anti-HCV)。结果:结果显示,孕妇中病毒性肝炎感染的总体血清流行率为1.02%,其中乙型肝炎病毒(HBV)感染率高于丙型肝炎病毒(HCV)。HBsAg的血清流行率为0.94%(12/1273)。与之前的一项本地研究相比,本研究显示孕妇中HBV和HCV感染率显著下降(HBV为0.94% vs 4.42%,HCV为0.08% vs 1.15%)。逻辑回归分析显示,肝炎家族史和流产史均与HBV血清阳性显著相关(OR = 12.77,P = 0.001;OR = 9.24,P = 0.0009)。结论:肝炎家族史和流产史与孕妇HBV血清阳性显著相关,支持实施强有力的产前筛查程序和提高对疾病结果的认识。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在明确孕妇中肝炎的当前血清流行率,并与以往的本地数据进行比较,同时确定与结果相关的潜在风险因素。病毒性肝炎是全球健康负担,也是伊拉克的流行病,其患病率之前已有记录。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究是一项基于医院的横断面研究,于2024年2月1日至6月30日进行,涉及14至45岁的1273名孕妇。
analysis_zh.methods: 通过简短的问卷收集人口统计数据,并使用Combo Rapid Test Strips对血液样本进行检测,以筛查乙型肝炎病毒表面抗原(HBsAg)和丙型肝炎病毒抗体(anti-HCV)。
analysis_zh.main_results: 结果显示,孕妇中病毒性肝炎感染的总体血清流行率为1.02%,其中乙型肝炎病毒(HBV)感染率高于丙型肝炎病毒(HCV)。HBsAg的血清流行率为0.94%(12/1273)。与之前的一项本地研究相比,本研究显示孕妇中HBV和HCV感染率显著下降(HBV为0.94% vs 4.42%,HCV为0.08% vs 1.15%)。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 肝炎家族史和流产史与孕妇HBV血清阳性显著相关,支持实施强有力的产前筛查程序和提高对疾病结果的认识。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,孕妇中HBV和HCV感染率有所下降,这可能为制定监测和预防策略提供依据。肝炎家族史和流产史是HBV的重要风险因素,强调了需要有针对性的干预措施。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究的局限性在于其横断面设计,无法确定因果关系。样本量对于血清流行率的估计是足够的,但可能无法代表更广泛的人群。本研究未能提供高水平的证据强度。

papers.title: Resolved hepatitis B is associated with higher reactivation risk than chronic infection after chemoembolization for hepatocellular carcinoma
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND Transarterial chemoembolization (TACE) is a cornerstone treatment for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), yet the hepatitis B virus (HBV) reactivation risk, particularly among patients with prior infection, remains incompletely characterized, with international guidelines providing discordant risk classifications. We hypothesized that patients with resolved HBV infection undergoing TACE face a higher reactivation risk than currently estimated by international guidelines. AIM To determine the incidence and risk factors of HBV reactivation in patients undergoing TACE for HBV-related HCC. METHODS We retrospectively analyzed patients who underwent TACE for HBV-related HCC at a tertiary hospital during 2007-2025. Patients receiving baseline antiviral therapy were excluded. Patients with definitive serostatus (n = 774) were stratified into chronic-infection [hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg)-positive, n = 727] and resolved-infection (HBsAg-negative/anti-hepatitis B core antibody-positive, n = 47) groups. Cumulative incidences and risk factors were assessed using Kaplan-Meier analysis and Cox regression, with robustness evaluated through multiple imputation, competing-risks, and antiviral-naive sensitivity analyses. RESULTS During a median follow-up of 16.7 months, HBV reactivation occurred in 60 patients (6.1% overall). Patients with resolved HBV status had a higher reactivation rate (21.3% vs 6.9%; P CONCLUSION HBV reactivation occurred in approximately 6% of patients undergoing TACE, with resolved infection status conferring > 3-fold higher risk and reactivation incidence exceeding 20%. These findings support prophylactic antiviral therapy rather than monitoring alone for HBsAg-negative/anti-hepatitis B core antibody-positive patients undergoing TACE.

papers.title_zh: 乙肝清除后肝细胞癌经动脉化疗栓塞治疗后的再激活风险高于慢性感染
papers.source_body_en: BACKGROUND Transarterial chemoembolization (TACE) is a cornerstone treatment for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), yet the hepatitis B virus (HBV) reactivation risk, particularly among patients with prior infection, remains incompletely characterized, with international guidelines providing discordant risk classifications. We hypothesized that patients with resolved HBV infection undergoing TACE face a higher reactivation risk than currently estimated by international guidelines. AIM To determine the incidence and risk factors of HBV reactivation in patients undergoing TACE for HBV-related HCC. METHODS We retrospectively analyzed patients who underwent TACE for HBV-related HCC at a tertiary hospital during 2007-2025. Patients receiving baseline antiviral therapy were excluded. Patients with definitive serostatus (n = 774) were stratified into chronic-infection [hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg)-positive, n = 727] and resolved-infection (HBsAg-negative/anti-hepatitis B core antibody-positive, n = 47) groups. Cumulative incidences and risk factors were assessed using Kaplan-Meier analysis and Cox regression, with robustness evaluated through multiple imputation, competing-risks, and antiviral-naive sensitivity analyses. RESULTS During a median follow-up of 16.7 months, HBV reactivation occurred in 60 patients (6.1% overall). Patients with resolved HBV status had a higher reactivation rate (21.3% vs 6.9%; P CONCLUSION HBV reactivation occurred in approximately 6% of patients undergoing TACE, with resolved infection status conferring > 3-fold higher risk and reactivation incidence exceeding 20%. These findings support prophylactic antiviral therapy rather than monitoring alone for HBsAg-negative/anti-hepatitis B core antibody-positive patients undergoing TACE.
papers.abstract_zh: 背景 经动脉化疗栓塞(TACE)是肝细胞癌(HCC)的基石治疗,然而乙型肝炎病毒(HBV)再激活风险,尤其是在既往感染患者中,仍未被完全阐明,国际指南对其风险分类存在不一致。我们假设,既往感染已解决的HBV患者接受TACE后的再激活风险高于国际指南目前的估计。目的 确定接受TACE治疗HBV相关HCC患者的HBV再激活发病率和危险因素。方法 我们回顾性分析了2007-2025年间在三级医院接受TACE治疗的HBV相关HCC患者。接受基线抗病毒药物治疗的患者被排除。具有明确血清学状态的患者(n = 774)被分为慢性感染组[乙型肝炎表面抗原(HBsAg)阳性,n = 727]和已解决感染组(HBsAg阴性/抗乙型肝炎核心抗体阳性,n = 47)。累积发病率和危险因素采用Kaplan-Meier分析和Cox回归进行评估,稳健性通过多重插补、竞争风险和抗病毒药物无敏感性分析进行评价。结果 在中位随访16.7个月期间,HBV再激活发生在60例患者(总体6.1%)。已解决HBV状态的患者再激活率更高(21.3% 对比 6.9%;P < 0.001)。多因素分析确定已解决的HBV感染(调整风险比:3.42;95% CI:2.11-5.54;P < 0.001)为独立危险因素。结论 接受TACE的患者中约6%发生HBV再激活,已解决感染状态使风险增加超过3倍,再激活发病率超过20%。这些结果支持对HBsAg阴性/抗乙型肝炎核心抗体阳性且接受TACE的患者进行预防性抗病毒药物治疗,而非仅监测。

papers.title: From virological selection to immune stratification: Hepatitis B virus-specific T cells for precision pegylated interferon therapy in chronic hepatitis B
papers.abstract: Pegylated interferon (PEG-IFN) alpha, an important agent for chronic hepatitis B (CHB), exerts antiviral and immunomodulatory activities and serves as a core therapy to pursue functional cure. However, there are significant individual differences in treatment response, and the lack of reliable patient-selection strategies remains a major limitation to clinical application. Recent studies have shown that hepatitis B virus (HBV)-specific T cells are the core effector cells mediating viral clearance and maintaining immune control, and that the degree of their functional restoration is closely related to responses to PEG-IFN treatment and hepatitis B surface antigen clearance. In chronic HBV infection, HBV-specific T cells generally exhibit characteristics such as reduced numbers, functional exhaustion, metabolic abnormalities, and epigenetic remodeling. PEG-IFN can achieve immune remodeling by enhancing HBV-specific T cell responses, promoting the formation of memory-like T cells, improving multifunctional effector functions, and partially reversing the exhausted state. This review summarizes HBV-specific T cell dysfunction in chronic HBV infection, PEG-IFN-mediated immune remodeling mechanisms and relevant biomarker advances, to discuss the value of these T cells for precise interferon candidate screening and immune-stratified therapy. Such indicators may transform CHB management from virology-based to immunology-guided strategies and support precision treatment toward functional cure.

papers.title_original: From virological selection to immune stratification: Hepatitis B virus-specific T cells for precision pegylated interferon therapy in chronic hepatitis B

analysis.scope_and_question: The review addresses chronic hepatitis B in humans and evaluates pegylated interferon‐α therapy, focusing on how HBV‐specific T‐cell status can be used to select patients for precision interferon treatment.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: This article is presented as a narrative review that summarizes existing knowledge on HBV‐specific T‐cell dysfunction, PEG‐IFN‐mediated immune remodeling, and emerging biomarkers, without reporting systematic search methods or meta‐analysis.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Authors agree that HBV‐specific T cells are the principal effectors of viral clearance, that PEG‐IFN can enhance their function and partially reverse exhaustion, and that measuring these immune parameters could guide individualized therapy.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The authors note substantial inter‐individual variability in response to PEG‐IFN and the current absence of validated patient‐selection biomarkers, and they highlight incomplete understanding of the mechanisms underlying T‐cell exhaustion and metabolic abnormalities in chronic HBV.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Future work should develop and validate immune‐based biomarkers of HBV‐specific T‐cell restoration to shift chronic hepatitis B management from virology‐centric to immunology‐guided precision treatment.

analysis.summary_en: This abstract‐level review examines chronic hepatitis B and the role of pegylated interferon‐α, proposing that HBV‐specific T‐cell profiling could enable precision therapy. It summarizes current knowledge of T‐cell dysfunction and PEG‐IFN‐driven immune remodeling, emphasizing consensus that these immune cells are central to viral clearance and that interferon can partially restore their activity. However, the authors highlight major gaps, including marked variability in treatment response and a lack of validated biomarkers to guide patient selection. They call for research to develop immune‐based markers that would transform management from a virology‐focused approach to one guided by host immunity, supporting individualized interferon treatment strategies.

papers.abstract_zh: 聚乙二醇化干扰素α(PEG-IFN)是慢性乙型肝炎(CHB)的重要药物,具有抗病毒药物和免疫调节活性,并作为实现功能性治愈的核心治疗手段。然而,治疗应答存在显著的个体差异,且缺乏可靠的患者筛选策略仍是临床应用的主要限制。最新研究表明,乙型肝炎病毒(HBV)特异性T细胞是介导病毒清除和维持免疫控制的核心效应细胞,其功能恢复程度与PEG-IFN 治疗应答以及乙型肝炎表面抗原清除密切相关。在慢性HBV感染中,HBV特异性T细胞通常表现为数量减少、功能衰竭、代谢异常和表观遗传重塑等特征。PEG-IFN可通过增强HBV特异性T细胞应答、促进记忆样T细胞的形成、提升多功能效应功能以及部分逆转衰竭状态,实现免疫重塑。本综述总结了慢性HBV感染中HBV特异性T细胞功能障碍、PEG-IFN介导的免疫重塑机制及相关生物标志物的进展,旨在探讨这些T细胞在精准干扰素候选筛选和免疫分层治疗中的价值。这些指标可能将CHB管理从基于病毒学的模式转变为免疫学指导的策略,并支持精准治疗向功能性治愈的实现。
papers.summary_zh: 聚乙二醇化干扰素α(PEG-IFN)是慢性乙型肝炎(CHB)的重要药物,具有抗病毒药物和免疫调节活性,并作为实现功能性治愈的核心治疗手段。然而,治疗应答存在显著的个体差异,且缺乏可靠的患者筛选策略仍是临床应用的主要限制。最新研究表明,乙型肝炎病毒(HBV)特异性T细胞是介导病毒清除和维持免疫控制的核心效应细胞,其功能恢复程度与PEG-IFN 治疗应答以及乙型肝炎表面抗原清除密切相关。在慢性HBV感染中,HBV特异性T细胞通常表现为数量减少、功能衰竭、代谢异常和表观遗传重塑等特征。PEG-IFN可通过增强HBV特异性T细胞应答、促进记忆样T细胞的形成、提升多功能效应功能以及部分逆转衰竭状态,实现免疫重塑。本综述总结了慢性HBV感染中HBV特异性T细胞功能障碍、PEG-IFN介导的免疫重塑机制及相关生物标志物的进展,旨在探讨这些T细胞在精准干扰素候选筛选和免疫分层治疗中的价值。这些指标可能将CHB管理从基于病毒学的模式转变为免疫学指导的策略,并支持精准治疗向功能性治愈的实现。

analysis_zh.scope_and_question: 本文回顾了人类慢性乙型肝炎中PEG-IFN-α治疗的情况,重点评估了HBV特异性T细胞状态如何用于选择精准干扰素治疗的患者。
analysis_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 本文以综述形式呈现,总结了HBV特异性T细胞功能障碍、PEG-IFN介导的免疫重塑和新兴生物标志物的知识,但未报告系统检索方法或meta分析。
analysis_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 作者一致认为,HBV特异性T细胞是病毒清除的主要效应细胞,PEG-IFN可以增强其功能并部分逆转耗竭,测量这些免疫参数可以指导个体化治疗。
analysis_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 作者指出,对PEG-IFN反应存在显著个体差异,目前缺乏验证的患者选择生物标志物,并强调对T细胞耗竭和慢性HBV中代谢异常机制的理解尚不完全。
analysis_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 未来的研究应开发并验证HBV特异性T细胞恢复的免疫生物标志物,以将慢性乙型肝炎管理从病毒学导向转变为免疫学导向的精准治疗。

Regional Events Focused on Oncology and Population Health Advertisement Opinion|Videos|September 17, 2026 Weighing Efficacy and Safety Data for an Emerging Hepatitis B Therapy Author(s)Raymond Chung, MD, Robert G. Gish, MD A roughly 20% functional cure rate is meaningful, but it comes with a safety profile that demands scrutiny in patients already doing well on suppressive therapy. This episode weighs that tradeoff. Advertisement Episodes in this series Previous slideNext slide EP. 1 Understanding the Immune Pathophysiology Driving Chronic Hepatitis B EP. 2 Hepatitis B Epidemiology: Closing the Screening and Diagnosis Gap EP. 3 Monitoring Disease Progression and Liver Cancer Risk in Hepatitis B EP. 4 Quantitative HBsAg Testing and the Path to Finite-Duration Therapy EP. 5 Unmet Needs and Long-Term Antiviral Safety in Hepatitis B Care EP. 6 Why Hepatitis B and Hepatitis C Cures Are Fundamentally Different EP. 7 The Next Frontier in Hepatitis B Functional and Virologic Cure EP. 8 Rethinking Standard of Care and the Promise of Functional Cure EP. 9 How Bepirovirsen Targets the Hepatitis B Viral Lifecycle EP. 10 Inside the Be-Well Trials: Design, Population, and Patient Selection Now Playing EP. 11 Weighing Efficacy and Safety Data for an Emerging Hepatitis B Therapy EP. 12 Capsid Assembly Modulators and the Case for Combination Therapy "Weighing Efficacy and Safety Data for an Emerging Hepatitis B Therapy" takes up how the panel balances a promising cure rate against a real safety signal. Dr. Chung notes that data across two trials pointed to a functional cure rate of roughly 20% in this patient group and asks Dr. Gish to react to those findings and weigh the efficacy signal against safety considerations in a population that is already well suppressed and feeling well on long-term nucleoside therapy. Dr. Gish describes himself as the optimist in a class that is one-third full or two-thirds empty, noting that nearly every patient he sees with hepatitis B asks when they might be able to stop treatment. He believes most patients already understand the functional cure concept and considers this therapy a genuine leap forward, though not yet approved and still pending FDA review. He compares the side effect profile to interferon therapy, an agent he and Dr. Chung both have extensive experience treating. He notes that 70% of patients on placebo in the Be-Well studies also experienced significant adverse events, suggesting hepatitis B itself, as a disease, contributes meaningfully to how patients feel. He considers grade 3 adverse events the more meaningful safety threshold, occurring in 16% of bepirovirsen recipients versus 3% on placebo, likely reflecting an immunologic response tied to ALT flares that he views as probably beneficial. He adds that kidney and bone marrow monitoring will be necessary, requiring meaningful clinical infrastructure. Asked which patients he sees as the best candidates once the therapy is approved, Dr. Gish points to three criteria: non-cirrhotic status, a favorable surface antigen window, and patient motivation, noting that more than half of his patients are already asking about this emerging data and preparing for that conversation. The next episode in this series, "Capsid Assembly Modulators and the Case for Combination Therapy," shifts to a different class of investigational therapy. Advertisement Episodes in this series Previous slideNext slide EP. 1 Understanding the Immune Pathophysiology Driving Chronic Hepatitis B EP. 2 Hepatitis B Epidemiology: Closing the Screening and Diagnosis Gap EP. 3 Monitoring Disease Progression and Liver Cancer Risk in Hepatitis B EP. 4 Quantitative HBsAg Testing and the Path to Finite-Duration Therapy EP. 5 Unmet Needs and Long-Term Antiviral Safety in Hepatitis B Care EP. 6 Why Hepatitis B and Hepatitis C Cures Are Fundamentally Different EP. 7 The Next Frontier in Hepatitis B Functional and Virologic Cure EP. 8 Rethinking Standard of Care and the Promise of Functional Cure EP. 9 How Bepirovirsen Targets the Hepatitis B Viral Lifecycle EP. 10 Inside the Be-Well Trials: Design, Population, and Patient Selection Now Playing EP. 11 Weighing Efficacy and Safety Data for an Emerging Hepatitis B Therapy EP. 12 Capsid Assembly Modulators and the Case for Combination Therapy "Weighing Efficacy and Safety Data for an Emerging Hepatitis B Therapy" takes up how the panel balances a promising cure rate against a real safety signal. Dr. Chung notes that data across two trials pointed to a functional cure rate of roughly 20% in this patient group and asks Dr. Gish to react to those findings and weigh the efficacy signal against safety considerations in a population that is already well suppressed and feeling well on long-term nucleoside therapy. Dr. Gish describes himself as the optimist in a class that is one-third full or two-thirds empty, noting that nearly every patient he sees with hepatitis B asks when they might be able to stop treatment. He believes most patients already understand the functional cure concept and considers this therapy a genuine leap forward, though not yet approved and still pending FDA review. He compares the side effect profile to interferon therapy, an agent he and Dr. Chung both have extensive experience treating. He notes that 70% of patients on placebo in the Be-Well studies also experienced significant adverse events, suggesting hepatitis B itself, as a disease, contributes meaningfully to how patients feel. He considers grade 3 adverse events the more meaningful safety threshold, occurring in 16% of bepirovirsen recipients versus 3% on placebo, likely reflecting an immunologic response tied to ALT flares that he views as probably beneficial. He adds that kidney and bone marrow monitoring will be necessary, requiring meaningful clinical infrastructure. Asked which patients he sees as the best candidates once the therapy is approved, Dr. Gish points to three criteria: non-cirrhotic status, a favorable surface antigen window, and patient motivation, noting that more than half of his patients are already asking about this emerging data and preparing for that conversation. The next episode in this series, "Capsid Assembly Modulators and the Case for Combination Therapy," shifts to a different class of investigational therapy. news.content_title: Researchers identify ANKRD11 as a brake on T-cell responses to chronic hepatitis B virus and cancer
news.content: Advanced Search Home News Releases Multimedia Meetings Login Register News Release 13-Sep-2026 Researchers identify ANKRD11 as a brake on T-cell responses to chronic hepatitis B virus and cancer Peer-Reviewed Publication Chinese Academy of Sciences Headquarters Facebook X LinkedIn WeChat Bluesky Message WhatsApp Email image: Proposed dynamics of antigen-specific CD8+ T cell populations regulated by Ankrd11 in chronic infection and cancer view more Credit: ZHOU Xuyu's group A research team led by Prof. ZHOU Xuyu from the Institute of Microbiology of the Chinese Academy of Sciences (CAS), in collaboration with researchers from Beijing Ditan Hospital and Capital Medical University, has identified ANKRD11 as a key regulator that reduces the activity of CD8+ T cells during chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection and cancer. The researchers found that ANKRD11 suppresses the AP-1 signaling pathway, which usually helps CD8+ T cells mount effective responses against infections and tumors. The study was published in Nature Immunology on September 11. HBV infects about 296 million people worldwide and is a leading cause of serious liver diseases such as cirrhosis and liver cancer. One major reason the immune system in controling chronic HBV is that CD8+ T cells, which normally attack infected cells, lose their strength and can't multiply well. The liver environment can further suppress immune responses, making some existing immune-based therapies less effective against HBV. Identifying new ways to restore T cell function is therefore an important goal in the treatment of chronic HBV infection. Building on their previous work, the researchers had developed a mouse model that mimics key features of human immune responses to HBV and identified a major target of the antiviral immune response. In the new study, they used advanced genetic tools to look across the whole genome and identify genes that might affect how T cells respond to chronic HBV. Among the candidate genes, they focused on Ankrd11 because it was new, showed strong results, and made sense as a regulator of how genes are turned on or off in immune cells. Deleting Ankrd11 specifically in T cells did not affect their development, but substantially enhanced their ability to fight infection. The modified T cells produced higher levels of key immune molecules and were more effective at attacking infected and cancerous cells. Further analysis showed that genes involved in T cell function were more readily activated in the absence of ANKRD11, indicating that the protein acts as a brake on T cell activity. The researchers also found that ANKRD11-deficient T cells were more resistant to signals that normally suppress immune responses. The reserchers then tested their findings in several disease models. In mice with HBV, removing Ankrd11 from T cells led to more active immune cells in the liver, helped clear the virus, and improved disease outcomes. In another virus model and in a cancer model, T cells without Ankrd11 could better fight the virus and shrink tumors—even in cases where other treatments had failed. The researchers also found that combining this approach with existing therapies made the treatment even stronger. The findings identify ANKRD11 as an important regulator that restrains T cell responses against chronic viral infection and cancer. Targeting ANKRD11 could provide a potential strategy for strengthening the body's own immune response to chronic HBV infection and cancer, particularly in cases where existing therapies are insufficient. news.content_original: Advanced Search Home News Releases Multimedia Meetings Login Register News Release 13-Sep-2026 Researchers identify ANKRD11 as a brake on T-cell responses to chronic hepatitis B virus and cancer Peer-Reviewed Publication Chinese Academy of Sciences Headquarters Facebook X LinkedIn WeChat Bluesky Message WhatsApp Email image: Proposed dynamics of antigen-specific CD8+ T cell populations regulated by Ankrd11 in chronic infection and cancer view more Credit: ZHOU Xuyu's group A research team led by Prof. ZHOU Xuyu from the Institute of Microbiology of the Chinese Academy of Sciences (CAS), in collaboration with researchers from Beijing Ditan Hospital and Capital Medical University, has identified ANKRD11 as a key regulator that reduces the activity of CD8+ T cells during chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection and cancer. The researchers found that ANKRD11 suppresses the AP-1 signaling pathway, which usually helps CD8+ T cells mount effective responses against infections and tumors. The study was published in Nature Immunology on September 11. HBV infects about 296 million people worldwide and is a leading cause of serious liver diseases such as cirrhosis and liver cancer. One major reason the immune system in controling chronic HBV is that CD8+ T cells, which normally attack infected cells, lose their strength and can't multiply well. The liver environment can further suppress immune responses, making some existing immune-based therapies less effective against HBV. Identifying new ways to restore T cell function is therefore an important goal in the treatment of chronic HBV infection. Building on their previous work, the researchers had developed a mouse model that mimics key features of human immune responses to HBV and identified a major target of the antiviral immune response. In the new study, they used advanced genetic tools to look across the whole genome and identify genes that might affect how T cells respond to chronic HBV. Among the candidate genes, they focused on Ankrd11 because it was new, showed strong results, and made sense as a regulator of how genes are turned on or off in immune cells. Deleting Ankrd11 specifically in T cells did not affect their development, but substantially enhanced their ability to fight infection. The modified T cells produced higher levels of key immune molecules and were more effective at attacking infected and cancerous cells. Further analysis showed that genes involved in T cell function were more readily activated in the absence of ANKRD11, indicating that the protein acts as a brake on T cell activity. The researchers also found that ANKRD11-deficient T cells were more resistant to signals that normally suppress immune responses. The reserchers then tested their findings in several disease models. In mice with HBV, removing Ankrd11 from T cells led to more active immune cells in the liver, helped clear the virus, and improved disease outcomes. In another virus model and in a cancer model, T cells without Ankrd11 could better fight the virus and shrink tumors—even in cases where other treatments had failed. The researchers also found that combining this approach with existing therapies made the treatment even stronger. The findings identify ANKRD11 as an important regulator that restrains T cell responses against chronic viral infection and cancer. Targeting ANKRD11 could provide a potential strategy for strengthening the body's own immune response to chronic HBV infection and cancer, particularly in cases where existing therapies are insufficient. supplementary_news.content_title: Trump’s surgeon general nominee Nicole Saphier praises MMR and hepatitis B vaccines in Senate hearing
supplementary_news.content: On Wednesday President Donald Trump's latest nominee for surgeon general took steps to distance herself from the president's false statements on vaccinations by telling a Senate confirmation hearing that the shots are not the cause of autism. Trump announced the nomination of Nicole Saphier, a radiologist and Fox News personality, for the country's top public health position in April—she is the third nominee for the role since the second Trump administration began. Saphier replaced wellness influencer Casey Means, who had drawn fire from a bipartisan group of lawmakers for her stances toward vaccines and alternative medicine. During her testimony on Wednesday, Saphier tried to create distance between herself and positions taken by both Trump and U.S. Health and Human Services (HHS) Secretary Robert Kennedy, Jr. Saphier told lawmakers that she does not know what causes autism, and she has "not seen reputable evidence that would suggest that vaccines cause autism." Sign up for Today in Science, a free daily newsletter from Scientific American and join a community of science-loving readers. When questioned about Trump's recent claim that the mumps, measles and rubella vaccine may be "lethal," Saphier responded by describing the shot as "our greatest tool for combating measles." Almost 3,300 cases of measles have been confirmed in the U.S. this year as of September 11, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention—an increase of more than 1,000 compared with the cases reported for all of 2025. Four deaths have been linked to the current outbreak, the most since 1992. When asked for comment, White House spokesperson Kush Desai called Saphier an "accomplished physician who has practiced radiology at Memorial Sloan Kettering and has been an outspoken voice on breast cancer prevention, intrusive COVID-19 mandates, the politicization of science and the federal government's role in America's chronic disease epidemic. She has been a powerful asset for President Trump and works tirelessly to deliver on every facet of his MAHA agenda." Saphier also expressed support for universal hepatitis B vaccination at birth—a long-standing CDC recommendation that Kennedy and other top Trump health officials have taken steps to eliminate. "The hepatitis B vaccines are one of the most tangible ways we have to prevent cancer, and that is something that I absolutely am always excited about because it is so hard to prevent cancer in so many patients," she said, referring to the hepatitis B vaccine's protective effect against hepatitis-related liver cancers. Saphier's nomination has been criticized by several public health advocacy groups. In a statement issued on Wednesday, Defend Public Health coordinating committee member Julie Scofield said Saphier is "exactly the wrong person to be Surgeon General." "She has no background in public health, and it shows," Scofield said. "Saphier has argued that 'personal responsibility' is key to improving Americans' overall health—an idea that contradicts the basic tenets of public health, which recognize that our health is affected by many factors an individual simply can't control." At today's hearing, Saphier stressed the importance of Americans personally taking steps to reduce their chances of becoming ill and added that providing more information to the public on prevention will be a priority if she's confirmed. "There are small, tangible lifestyle modifications that people can do," Saphier said. "That doesn't mean that you have to become a nutrition expert or a someone who's at the gym every single day. supplementary_news.content: 18.09.2026 |Flights of «Türkmen howa ýollary» |Archive | Search Login Main News Shorts Articles Poster Business Media Ads Auto centers Directory Sport Payment Main News Shorts Articles Business Media Sport Payment Place an ad All categories Main /News /Health 18.03.2025 13710 Share on social network WHO strengthens medical professionals’ capacity in Turkmenistan on viral hepatitis B The World Health Organization (WHO) Country Office in Turkmenistan held a training course on the "Diagnostics and treatment of viral hepatitis B according to WHO recommendations and national protocol" from March 12 to 13, 2025. The course led by WHO/Europe consultant, Professor Alexander Nersesov, aims to enhance the capacity of Turkmen medical professionals in their effort to combat viral hepatitis B. The skill-building session was conducted at the Infectious disease treatment-prevention center in videoconference mode. The participants of the event were doctors specializing in the diagnosis and treatment of viral hepatitis from the Infectious disease treatment-prevention center of the Directorate of Infectious Diseases Centers, primary health care providers, infectious diseases specialists from the institutions at the district level, and representatives from the department of infectious diseases at the State Medical University named after Myrat Karryev. The training covered essential information on hepatitis B, its diagnosis, classification, and treatment, with specific guidance for chronic cases, pregnancy, and special patient groups, as well as hepatitis D. This training is designed to equip medical professionals with the updated knowledge and best practices in viral hepatitis B diagnosis and treatment, aligning with both WHO guidelines and national protocols. By enhancing the skills of healthcare providers, this initiative will contribute to improved patient outcomes and strengthen Turkmenistan's efforts to control and manage viral hepatitis. Here’s What You Should Know By Erica Selorm Kabe Health & Fitness THU, 17 SEP 2026 Have you ever heard someone say, “I’m blood group O, so I hardly get sick,” or wondered whether your blood group could protect you from certain diseases? Most of us know our blood groups mainly because of blood transfusion, pregnancy or blood donation. We are usually identified as blood group A, B, AB or O and as either Rh positive or Rh negative. But could these differences actually affect our chances of contracting infections such as HIV or Hepatitis B? It is an interesting question, and one that scientists have investigated. But there is an important message everyone should understand: your blood group should never be considered protection against HIV or Hepatitis B. What Does Your Blood Group Really Mean? Our ABO blood groups are determined by certain substances, known as antigens, found on the surface of red blood cells. People with blood group A have A antigens, those with group B have B antigens, people with AB have both, while people with blood group O have neither A nor B antigens. Scientists have studied these biological differences to determine whether they are associated with susceptibility to various diseases and infections. Some studies have reported associations between particular blood groups and certain diseases. However, finding an association does not mean that a particular blood group directly causes a disease or guarantees protection from it. What About HIV and Hepatitis B? HIV attacks the body's immune system. It can be transmitted through certain body fluids, including blood, semen, vaginal fluids and breast milk. It can also be transmitted from mother to child. HIV is not spread through ordinary contact such as hugging, shaking hands or sharing food. Hepatitis B is caused by the Hepatitis B virus (HBV), which attacks the liver. The infection can become chronic and, over time, may lead to serious complications such as liver cirrhosis and liver cancer. HBV can be transmitted through infected blood and other body fluids, during sex, through contaminated sharp instruments and from an infected mother to her baby. Because these infections interact with the human body in complex ways, researchers have investigated whether characteristics such as ABO and Rh blood groups are associated with differences in infection patterns. However, research findings have varied among different populations. Therefore, your blood group alone cannot reliably tell whether you will or will not contract HIV or Hepatitis B. Why This Matters in Ghana HIV remains an important public health issue in Ghana. According to Ghana's 2025 National HIV Estimates and Projections, more than 337,000 people were estimated to be living with HIV in the country. This makes accurate public information about HIV prevention particularly important. Hepatitis B is also a major health concern because a person can be infected without initially showing obvious symptoms. Chronic infection can eventually cause severe liver disease. These realities make prevention, testing and reliable health information far more useful than assumptions based on one's blood group. Don't Let Your Blood Group Give You False Confidence Whether you are blood group O, A, B or AB, positive or negative, you should not consider yourself naturally protected from HIV or Hepatitis B. For HIV, prevention includes knowing your status, practising safer sex, avoiding the sharing of contaminated needles and sharp objects, and using recommended preventive services such as pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) when appropriate. People living with HIV who receive effective antiretroviral treatment can live long and healthy lives. Effective treatment can also reduce the amount of HIV in the blood to an undetectable level, at which point HIV is not sexually transmitted. For Hepatitis B, there is another powerful preventive tool: vaccination. The World Health Organization identifies Hepatitis B vaccination as an effective way of preventing the infection. Testing is equally important. You cannot determine someone's HIV or Hepatitis B status simply by looking at them—or by knowing their blood group. Know Your Status, Not Just Your Blood Group There is nothing wrong with knowing whether you are A+, B+, AB-, O+ or any other blood type. That information is medically useful. But knowing your blood group should not replace knowing your HIV or Hepatitis B status. Scientific research into blood groups and infectious diseases helps us better understand how biological differences between individuals may relate to patterns of disease. However, for the general public, the practical message is simple: No blood group should be treated as a shield against HIV or Hepatitis B. Get tested when appropriate. Practise recommended preventive measures. Find out whether you have been adequately vaccinated against Hepatitis B and seek advice from a qualified healthcare professional where necessary. Your blood group may tell us something interesting about your biology, but when it comes to HIV and Hepatitis B, prevention, vaccination where available, testing and appropriate medical care remain far more important than the letter attached to your blood type. Research may continue to uncover interesting links between blood groups and different diseases, but one message remains clear: do not depend on your blood group to protect you. Depend on knowledge, prevention and timely healthcare. Know your blood group but more importantly, know your status and protect your health. Regional Events Focused on Oncology and Population Health Advertisement Opinion|Videos|September 17, 2026 Capsid Assembly Modulators and the Case for Combination Therapy Author(s)Raymond Chung, MD, Robert G. Gish, MD A newer generation of capsid assembly modulators may finally move the needle on surface antigen, something earlier compounds in this class could not achieve. This episode explores that shift. Advertisement Episodes in this series Previous slideNext slide EP. 1 Understanding the Immune Pathophysiology Driving Chronic Hepatitis B EP. 2 Hepatitis B Epidemiology: Closing the Screening and Diagnosis Gap EP. 3 Monitoring Disease Progression and Liver Cancer Risk in Hepatitis B EP. 4 Quantitative HBsAg Testing and the Path to Finite-Duration Therapy EP. 5 Unmet Needs and Long-Term Antiviral Safety in Hepatitis B Care EP. 6 Why Hepatitis B and Hepatitis C Cures Are Fundamentally Different EP. 7 The Next Frontier in Hepatitis B Functional and Virologic Cure EP. 8 Rethinking Standard of Care and the Promise of Functional Cure EP. 9 How Bepirovirsen Targets the Hepatitis B Viral Lifecycle EP. 10 Inside the Be-Well Trials: Design, Population, and Patient Selection EP. 11 Weighing Efficacy and Safety Data for an Emerging Hepatitis B Therapy Now Playing EP. 12 Capsid Assembly Modulators and the Case for Combination Therapy In "Capsid Assembly Modulators and the Case for Combination Therapy," the panel turns to a less mature but promising class of therapy targeting viral capsid assembly. Dr. Chung shifts to other, less mature classes of therapy, starting with pevifoscovir, also known as ALG-001075, describing in vitro data suggesting it works through several mechanisms, including direct antiviral activity blocking HBV DNA production, blocking cccDNA establishment, and potentially inhibiting e-antigen secretion. He asks Dr. Gish to explain its mechanism, how it compares with current standard of care, and how to interpret recent monotherapy findings showing sustained antigen reductions after 24 weeks of entecavir in a small cohort of e-antigen-positive patients. Dr. Gish says he has been excited about capsid assembly modulators, sometimes called CAMs or CpAMs, since this class emerged, describing pevifoscovir as a true second- or third-generation compound. He explains that this class includes drugs producing empty capsids and others producing aberrant capsids, both altering viral secretion and reducing infection of other cells, which decreases total viral replication and release. He notes that pevifoscovir's surface antigen data appear to be the first meaningful signal for this drug class, since an earlier compound in the same category did not affect surface antigen and saw resistance and relapse after stopping therapy. He believes pevifoscovir could compete directly against nucleoside analogs, which rarely reduce surface antigen meaningfully, achieving only about 5% at five years with entecavir or tenofovir-based regimens. He also describes cccDNA as constantly recycled and re-established in the nucleus, but notes that natural endonuclease activity degrades it over time, so interrupting that replenishment cycle may allow natural clearance. He credits earlier work suggesting this concept, though he believes pevifoscovir has stronger supporting data. Looking ahead, he expects combination regimens of two to four compounds, rather than any single agent, to ultimately deliver surface antigen clearance and functional cure. In "Can Innate Immune Agonists Help Deliver Hepatitis B Cure?," the panel will unpack a therapy working through an entirely different, innate immune pathway. 2026-09-15 雨露肝霖 雨露肝霖 发表于上海 慢性乙型肝炎 消化新前沿 企业/ 关注 互相关注 慢乙肝属于免疫介导疾病,免疫重建是治愈核心。联合治疗是未来方向,PegIFNα 兼具抗病毒与免疫调节,是临床治愈基石;新型降 HBsAg 药物免疫作用弱、易复发,推荐 PegIFNα 前置联合方案。 深度解析医学证据,DeepEvidence为你支撑决策 01 慢乙肝是免疫介导性疾病,免疫重建是实现治愈的关键 慢乙肝本质上是免疫介导性疾病, HBV破坏机体的先天免疫和适应性免疫,驱动感染慢性化,机体无法清除病毒,导致感染持续存在[1,2]。肝内cccDNA和整合HBV DNA及其持续产生的HBsAg等病毒抗原,导致先天免疫和适应性免疫受损。其中,HBV特异性CD8+ T细胞是清除HBV病毒的核心效应细胞[3],但因长期抗原暴露及肝脏耐受性微环境等因素发生功能障碍与耗竭[4],致使机体丧失清除HBV及受感染肝细胞的能力。持续HBV病毒复制与肝脏炎症损伤,进一步促进乙肝疾病进展。因此,重建对HBV的免疫应答是实现乙肝治愈的关键。 HBV及其产生的病毒抗原导致先天免疫和适应性免疫受损[2] 02 联合治疗是未来的必然趋势,免疫是持久临床治愈的核心 实现乙肝治愈的策略有两种途径,一是在不杀死受感染肝细胞的情况下治愈乙肝,如通过基因编辑、表观遗传修饰等清除或永久沉默cccDNA,目前还无法实现;二是诱导免疫调节,安全清除HBV感染的肝细胞。“降低病毒负荷”+“强效免疫调节”是未来实现临床治愈的必然趋势。 靶向HBV生命周期的药物,如ASO/siRNA虽然能够快速降低HBsAg,但几乎无免疫调节作用,停药后复发率高,难以实现持久的临床治愈。例如备受瞩目的ASO药物Bepirovirsen(GSK836)于2026年8月在日本正式获批上市,目前在中国上市时间仍然未知。本次日本获批依据两项全球多中心III期临床试验,B-Well 1和B-Well 2研究表明对于核苷经治100 ≤ HBsAg < 3000 IU/mL的慢乙肝患者,经Bepirovirsen联合NA治疗的临床治愈率分别为20%和19%[5]。需要客观看待的是,该药物适用人群存在明确限制,仍有大部分患者无法从中获益,而且HBsAg清除后的复阳率超过60%,其远期疗效与长期安全性仍有待真实世界数据进一步验证。 针对免疫调节的新型药物,比如治疗性疫苗、TLR7/8/9激动剂、单克隆抗体、PD-1/PD-L1抑制剂等目前疗效均有限。因此,只有强效的免疫调节,能有效激活先天免疫和适应性免疫,才是实现持久临床治愈的核心。 降低病毒负荷和宿主免疫重建的治疗策略[6] 03 PegIFNα具有强效免疫调节作用,是实现慢乙肝临床治愈的基石药物 聚乙二醇干扰素α(PegIFNα)是目前免疫调节作用最强效的乙肝药物,同时具有直接抗病毒和免疫调节的双重作用[7],因此是实现慢乙肝临床治愈的基石药物。在直接抗病毒方面,PegIFNα可通过直接抗病毒作用抑制HBV生命周期的全过程,降低HBV DNA、HBeAg、HBsAg、HBV RNA,更重要的是可降低cccDNA,从源头抑制病毒。在免疫调节方面,PegIFNα通过免疫重建,实现免疫清除,建立长期的免疫记忆,实现持久的临床治愈。 3.1 免疫重建——主动打破免疫耐受,激活机体免疫 PegIFNα协同激活先天与适应性免疫,实现对慢乙肝的免疫重建[8]。PegIFNα广泛调控多种免疫细胞:增强树突状细胞(DC)的抗原提呈能力,放大NK细胞应答、增强其细胞毒活性;通过诱导巨噬细胞等肝非实质细胞产生外泌体,强化整体抗病毒效应;提高浆细胞比例,促进抗病毒中和抗体生成;促进CD8+、CD4+ T淋巴细胞活化,进而提升细胞因子分泌水平与细胞毒性T淋巴细胞(CTL)应答效能。 PegIFNα实现对慢乙肝的免疫重建[8] 3.2 免疫清除——降低病毒负荷,清除受感染肝细胞 PegIFNα可通过非溶细胞性和溶细胞性两种途径清除HBV感染。非溶细胞性清除主要通过细胞因子可在不杀伤肝细胞的条件下抑制乃至清除HBV。溶细胞性清除是消除HBV最直接的方式,主要依赖细胞毒性T淋巴细胞的作用,并有NK和自然杀伤 T 细胞(NKT)等协同参与,杀伤受感染肝细胞,实现免疫清除。 清除HBV感染的主要途径[9] 3.3 免疫记忆——建立长期免疫,实现持久临床治愈 PegIFNα治疗可促进慢乙肝患者记忆T细胞的恢复,应答者在体外再次遇到病毒抗原时表现出快速而强烈的记忆应答[10]。同时,PegIFNα治疗可有效恢复HBsAg特异性B细胞的活化状态与IgG+ 经典记忆B细胞分化,并促进HBsAb产生[11],有利于临床治愈持久性。 3.4 临床治愈后多重获益 正是PegIFNα这种强效且持久的免疫调节机制,使得基于PegIFNα的治疗方案能使慢乙肝患者治疗获益最大化。一项III期临床治愈RCT研究显示,NAs经治患者基于PegIFNα-2b联合TDF治疗的临床治愈率达31.4%[12],临床治愈患者延长随访104周时的维持率高达约90%[13]。此外,临床治愈后具有多重获益,其肝脏内免疫环境明显改善[14],肝内cccDNA和整合HBV DNA显著降低[15,16],肝癌发生风险降至最低[17,18]。 04 讨 论 综合来看,未来联合治疗是实现乙肝临床治愈的必然趋势,“降低病毒负荷+强效免疫调节”是关键策略,免疫是持久临床治愈的核心。GSK836等新型药物的III期数据已经表明,缺乏强效持久免疫调节的药物,即使能在短期内降低HBsAg,停药复阳率高的问题仍无法解决。免疫调节剂如PD-1/PD-L1抑制剂、TLR激动剂等疗效十分有限。PegIFNα凭借其不可替代的免疫调节机制——免疫重建、免疫清除、免疫记忆,是目前最强效的免疫调节药物,因此是联合治疗的基石药物,未来不同药物如何联合、联合时机、具体疗程仍需要进一步探索。 先前GSK836序贯PegIFNα治疗的II期B-Together研究显示,更早序贯PegIFNα,复发率越低[19]。这提示更早开始PegIFNα治疗,可在一定量抗原暴露窗口下提升有效的免疫识别,重建对HBV的适应性免疫应答,才能实现对受感染肝细胞的持续清除及免疫控制,最终达到持久的临床治愈。因此,PegIFNα与ASO/siRNA的联合治疗策略应前置PegIFNα,让免疫重建先行,为后续的联合增效夯实基础。以PegIFNα巩固可建立长期的免疫记忆。 此外,PegIFNα与CAM、治疗性疫苗等的联合也值得进一步探索。未来需在机制协同的基础上,通过临床试验进一步明确联合时机、疗程长短与不同人群分层管理,真正将“降低病毒负荷+强效免疫调节”的核心策略转化为可落地的持久治愈方案。 参考文献: [1] Yuen MF, Chen DS, Dusheiko GM, et al. Now a team at the Institute of Microbiology of the Chinese Academy of Sciences, working with colleagues at Capital Medical University, has uncovered a molecular gatekeeper behind this decline. Reporting in Nature Immunology, Wei Xu and colleagues show that ANKRD11, a chromatin-associated protein, acts as a brake on CD8+ T cell effector differentiation, and that removing this brake dramatically enhances antiviral and antitumor immunity in mouse models. The study began with a practical problem: researchers have lacked good tools to study the behavior of hepatitis B virus-specific T cells in a physiologically relevant setting. The team used a humanized mouse model carrying the human HLA-A11 molecule to identify a T cell receptor that recognizes HBc141-151, an epitope from the hepatitis B core antigen that is clinically relevant in human patients. This receptor, which the authors call HB-I, allowed them to generate transgenic mice whose entire CD8+ T cell population is specific for a single, human-relevant HBV epitope, providing a tractable platform for dissecting why these cells fail during chronic infection. With that platform in hand, the researchers turned to an unbiased discovery strategy. Using a whole-genome CRISPR-Cas9 knockout library delivered into HBV-specific T cells, followed by screening under chronic antigen stimulation, they asked which genes, when deleted, would help T cells resist the dysfunctional state that normally develops. The screen converged on Ankrd11, a gene previously known as a chromatin regulator implicated in neural development and in Kabuki-like syndromes, but never before linked to T cell exhaustion. Loss of Ankrd11 consistently produced T cells that proliferated more vigorously and retained stronger effector characteristics. Discover more Cancer genes Medical Literature & Resources Genetic Disorders Biological Sciences The mechanistic picture that emerges from the paper is epigenetic. ANKRD11 appears to restrain the accessibility and acetylation of key effector genes. Using ATAC-seq, bulk RNA-seq and CUT&Tag profiling of the histone mark H3K27ac, the team showed that Ankrd11-deficient CD8+ T cells display increased chromatin openness and enhancer acetylation at loci encoding AP-1 family transcription factors, notably Fos and Fosb. Elevated AP-1 activity, in turn, drives a program of effector differentiation: the cells produce more granzyme B and interferon-gamma, resist the immunosuppressive conditions that normally silence them, and maintain function even when interleukin-2, a survival factor, is limiting. Functionally, the consequences of losing this brake were striking. In mice carrying a replicating HBV plasmid or infected with recombinant HBV vectors, Ankrd11-deficient HBV-specific T cells expanded more robustly, infiltrated the liver more effectively, and drastically reduced serum levels of hepatitis B surface antigen, viral DNA and markers of liver damage. Parallel experiments using a second chronic infection model, lymphocytic choriomeningitis virus clone 13, confirmed the generality of the effect: adoptively transferred Ankrd11-deficient virus-specific P14 T cells showed enhanced granzyme expression, proliferation and viral control in the spleen and blood. Perhaps the most conceptually interesting finding concerns the differentiation paths that exhausted T cells normally follow. In chronic infection and cancer, antigen-specific CD8+ T cells split into progenitor exhausted T cells, which express the transcription factor TCF-1 and serve as a self-renewing reservoir, and terminally exhausted T cells, which lose TCF-1 and are irreversibly dysfunctional. The authors found that Ankrd11 deficiency accelerates the conversion of progenitor exhausted cells into effector-like exhausted cells, but importantly, the resulting cells are cytotoxic and functional rather than inert. This suggests ANKRD11 does not simply maintain progenitor pools but actively gates how far exhausted cells differentiate toward effector competence. The study also revealed a distinct route of reprogramming specific to chronic hepatitis B. A large fraction of HBV-specific CD8+ T cells in tolerant mice carries a PD-1-negative, TOX-negative phenotype that has resisted conventional checkpoint-based rescue strategies. When ANKRD11-mediated repression was relieved, these tolerant cells differentiated into PD-1-positive, KLRG1-positive effector cells armed with high granzyme levels, providing an explanation for the improved viral clearance. In other words, ANKRD11 deficiency unlocks an otherwise dormant pool of virus-specific cells that immune checkpoint blockade alone cannot reach. Discover more Genetics Infectious Diseases gene Colleges & Universities Postdoc Position Listings The antitumor implications were tested directly in cancer models. Ankrd11-deficient CD8+ T cells promoted rejection of implanted tumors, enhanced intratumoral T cell activity, and acted synergistically with immune checkpoint blockade, potentiating the effect of PD-1 pathway inhibition. Given that the exhaustion of tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes is a central cause of immunotherapy failure, a single gene whose deletion reprograms effector differentiation under immunosuppressive conditions is an attractive candidate for therapeutic engineering, for example in chimeric antigen receptor or T cell receptor-engineered cell products. A provisional patent application has been filed based on the findings, underscoring the translational interest. Caveats remain before ANKRD11 targeting reaches the clinic. ANKRD11 is a broad chromatin regulator with established roles in neural and cardiac development, so systemic inhibition is unlikely to be safe; the therapeutic window will probably lie in ex vivo engineering of T cells or in carefully targeted delivery. It will also be important to determine whether accelerated terminal differentiation comes at the cost of long-term memory formation. Nevertheless, the study delivers a clear conceptual advance: T cell dysfunction in chronic infection and cancer is not merely the product of inhibitory receptor signaling, but is epigenetically authored, and specific chromatin factors such as ANKRD11 can be removed to rewrite that script. For the hundreds of millions of people living with chronic hepatitis B, and for cancer patients whose T cells have gone quiet, that insight opens a new direction for immunotherapy design. The concept of T cell exhaustion has shaped immunology for two decades. Since the landmark demonstration that chronically stimulated CD8+ T cells can regain function when inhibitory pathways are interrupted, researchers have catalogued a molecular signature of the dysfunctional state, and later work established the transcription factor TOX as a master architect of the exhaustion program, acting at both transcriptional and epigenetic levels. What has remained less clear is whether exhaustion is a fixed fate or a tunable state whose chromatin underpinnings can be deliberately rewritten. The new study adds weight to the second view by identifying a specific chromatin-associated protein whose removal shifts the balance of differentiation toward cytotoxic competence. The methodological route to this finding is worth noting. Genome-wide CRISPR-Cas9 knockout screens have become a powerful way to uncover genes that constrain or enable T cell behavior, and previous efforts using this approach identified regulators such as REGNASE-1 and Roquin as suppressors of effector expansion and antitumor immunity. The present screen extends this logic into the setting of chronic hepatitis B virus infection, a context in which suppressive cues differ from those in tumors and in which conventional checkpoint blockade has shown only modest clinical benefit. That an unbiased screen converged on a gene with no prior immunological pedigree illustrates how phenotype-first discovery can bypass assumptions rooted in known pathways. ANKRD11 itself carries an interesting dual history. It was first characterized as a chromatin regulator essential for neural development, and subsequent work showed it controls cardiac neural crest-mediated remodeling of the outflow tract. Its association with a Kabuki-like syndrome in humans reflects the pleiotropic consequences of disturbing a factor that operates broadly across tissues. This background both explains why the protein had escaped attention in immunology and reinforces the caution that any therapeutic interference must be confined to engineered cells rather than delivered systemically. The AP-1 connection provides a mechanistic bridge to earlier T cell biology. AP-1 family transcription factors, built from Fos and Jun proteins, have long been recognized as immediate-early responders to T cell receptor signaling, and their activity is known to cooperate with other factors to specify effector genes. By showing that ANKRD11 restrains chromatin accessibility and H3K27 acetylation at AP-1 loci, the study suggests a route by which a chromatin regulator can gate a transcriptional program that is otherwise primed and waiting in naive and exhausted cells alike. The authors have deposited the datasets underlying these conclusions in public repositories: bulk RNA-seq data under accession GSE299520, ATAC-seq data under GSE299519, and CUT&Tag data under GSE299521, with source data provided alongside the paper. No original code was generated. This transparency should allow groups working on T cell engineering to interrogate the chromatin changes directly and to test whether similar ANKRD11-sensitive programs operate in human tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes, a necessary step before the findings can inform next-generation cell therapy design.
